P-R5-1.measurement: part H (internal/domain/acceptance_w0601_step4h_test.go, 4 ids) owns it. W06-01-NEG-EFFECTS-SETUP-UNRESOLVED asserts unresolved() == 1 against a query on resource_effects latest-sequence rows in ('STARTED','UNKNOWN'); W06-01-NEG-EFFECTS-UNRECONCILED-REFUSED asserts [409,'STATE_CONFLICT','unknown effects require reconciliation; blind retry prohibited', 0] with the refusal string the card itself does not write (it is unique to durability.go:34); W06-01-NEG-EFFECTS-CONTROL-RECONCILED then asserts unresolved() == 0 after appending a DONE row for the same effect key, and W06-01-OUTPUT-EFFECTS-RECHECK-IS-INSIDE-THE-ACCEPTANCE-TRANSACTION asserts the identical request body lands [201 -> 'PASS','ACCEPTED', receipt delta 1]. So both halves the blocker demanded exist: refusal AND control, differential on one variable (the effect state), not on the request. I re-ran the four rows green (EXIT=0, 4/4 PASS) and I re-measured the falsifier: muting the :108 branch (keep the call, never take the refusal) turns exactly W06-01-NEG-EFFECTS-UNRECONCILED-REFUSED red with actual [201,null,null,1] and EXIT=1 - the acceptance lands when the guard is gone. This is the second independent identity to establish that :108 is reachable, refusing and falsifiable inside this card's write_scope; the round-5 excuse text is no longer the live record because precision_notes_round5_findings.json S-1 retracts it and the frozen part-G row was left unedited (1 touching commit).

P-R5-2.round5_statement: blocker - (a) the F4 mechanism string about :208 was published false and uncorrected, (b) the V7b :67 survivor reason was published false, (c) F4's rStatus/aStatus expected terms were structurally frozen to 0.

P-R5-2.measurement: (a)+(c): part I (acceptance_w0601_step4i_test.go, 5 ids) is the replacement the blocker described. Each of the five rows calls its route unconditionally - `cStatus, created, _ = f.request(...)`, `rStatus, restricted, _ = ...`, `tStatus, terminal, _ = ...`, `aStatus, foreign, _ = ...` - so no expected term is guaranteed by control flow, contrast part F where `rStatus := 0` / `aStatus := 0` are assigned only inside `if cStatus == 201` and `if rStatus == 200` and therefore can only ever be 0 while cStatus measures 403. The rows fail for the reason they name and I located each named owner on disk: 403 'restricted reference unavailable' is emitted by http.go:161-162 (visibleAs, i.e. grant/visibility), not by any isolation rule; the RESTRICTED class dies at protected_artifacts.go:124 schema validation -> 400 'request violates CreateArtifactRequest schema' and never reaches a guard; the executor's second /report dies at runtime.go:182 -> 409 'run already terminal'; and the acceptance naming the never-created artifact dies at acceptance.go:222 -> 422 'exact output artifact vector required', i.e. before :208 is read. Row 5 is a positive control that accepts (201,'PASS','ACCEPTED', receipt delta 1), so the four refusals cannot be blamed on a broken fixture. S-6 in precision_notes_round6_findings.json corrects the mechanism string to exactly that ordering-plus-closure account and states in 'what_this_does_NOT_claim' that it does NOT give :208 a falsifying id. (b): precision_notes_round5_findings.json S-3 drops the executor's 'coverage gap, not defence in depth' label and adopts the reviewer measurement. Residual gap, filed as P-R6-4-adjacent: S-3 does not restate the decisive half of round 5's finding - that faulting :31 reddens W06-01-NEG-RECHECK-POLICY-MOVED-REFUSED while faulting :67 reddens nothing - so a reader still cannot see which clause decides; and round 5's demanded note about the STALE-REPORT asymmetry is absent.
